note: Offline context for the selector: which catalogue variables can speak to a phenomenon, in which role, with which limits, and what cannot be answered. This is context, NOT a whitelist: any phenomenon text is accepted, and a phenomenon that is not listed is judged against concepts.json. Roles describe curated relevance, not causality shown by the data.

roles.core_indicator: the variable in which the phenomenon itself is defined or measured
roles.related_condition: an environmental condition that drives or modulates the phenomenon
roles.response: a variable that is expected to respond to the phenomenon

phenomena.label: Drought
phenomena.description: A prolonged shortage of water relative to normal conditions. Meteorological drought is a precipitation deficit; agricultural drought a soil moisture deficit; hydrological drought a deficit in runoff and storage. The types develop on different time scales and are not interchangeable.

variable_links.statement: A precipitation deficit relative to the local climatology defines meteorological drought and is the input of the SPI.
variable_links.limits: Monthly regional means; says nothing about water demand, storage or impacts.

variable_links.statement: A root-zone soil moisture deficit is what agricultural drought refers to.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Higher atmospheric evaporative demand increases drought severity for a given precipitation deficit.
variable_links.limits: Model diagnostic with a known trend drift in GLDAS-2.1.

variable_links.statement: Vapour pressure deficit is the atmospheric dryness that plants experience during drought.
variable_links.limits: Derived from forcing fields.

variable_links.statement: Temperature raises evaporative demand and therefore affects drought severity.
variable_links.limits: A monthly mean; temperature alone does not indicate drought.

variable_links.statement: Reduced runoff and streamflow characterise hydrological drought.
variable_links.limits: Modelled runoff generation, not gauged river discharge.

variable_links.statement: Terrestrial water storage integrates multi-year deficits in groundwater, soil and surface water.
variable_links.limits: About 300 km resolution; includes human withdrawals and ice changes, not only drought.

variable_links.statement: Evapotranspiration falls when soil moisture becomes limiting.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate; can also rise early in a drought when demand is high and water is still available.

variable_links.statement: Vegetation greenness declines under high vapour pressure deficit and water stress.
variable_links.limits: Greenness also responds to land use, irrigation and temperature.

unanswerable_notes: Recorded drought events or official declarations: no event catalogue has been delivered.
The SPI is a derived meteorological drought index; it does not show that agricultural, hydrological or socio-economic drought occurred.
Streamflow, reservoir and groundwater-level drought: no gauge or well data are prepared.
No evapotranspiration-based drought index (e.g. SPEI) is registered as a recipe.

phenomena.label: Flood
phenomena.description: Water covering land that is normally dry. Floods are events of hours to weeks that depend on rainfall intensity, antecedent wetness, snowmelt, river routing, tides and human infrastructure.

variable_links.statement: Heavy precipitation is a main driver of floods, but floods also depend on antecedent conditions and catchment properties.
variable_links.limits: A monthly regional mean cannot resolve the rainfall intensity or duration of a flood; it must not be read as flood frequency.

variable_links.statement: Wet antecedent soil increases the share of rainfall that becomes runoff.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters. Monthly means only.

variable_links.statement: Runoff generation describes how much water the land sheds in wet months.
variable_links.limits: Modelled monthly runoff generation, not river discharge or water level; no routing or flood extent.

variable_links.statement: Snowmelt contributes to floods in snow-affected catchments.
variable_links.limits: Modelled snowpack; monthly means do not resolve melt events.

unanswerable_notes: Flood frequency, duration and severity need a recorded flood event catalogue with coverage information; none has been delivered (data_required).
No approved recipe derives flood events from monthly data: monthly precipitation, runoff or storage anomalies are not flood counts.
Flood extent, river discharge and water level are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Heavy precipitation
phenomena.description: Precipitation events of high intensity. They are defined from daily or sub-daily amounts.

variable_links.statement: Monthly precipitation shows whether months have become wetter or drier overall.
variable_links.limits: Heavy precipitation is defined on daily or sub-daily data; a monthly mean cannot show a change in intensity or in the number of heavy-rain days.

unanswerable_notes: Frequency and intensity of heavy precipitation need daily or sub-daily precipitation, which is not prepared.
No approved recipe for extreme-precipitation indices is registered.

phenomena.label: Warming / temperature rise
phenomena.description: A long-term increase in temperature of the air, the land surface or the sea surface.

variable_links.statement: Near-surface air temperature is the standard variable for describing warming over land.
variable_links.limits: Analysis-based forcing field starting in 2000; a 25-year record is short for climate trends.

variable_links.statement: Sea surface temperature describes warming of the ocean surface.
variable_links.limits: Ocean regions only.

variable_links.statement: Land surface skin temperature follows the surface energy balance and usually warms with the air.
variable_links.limits: Model skin temperature; differs from air temperature over dry land.

variable_links.statement: Satellite daytime land surface temperature is an independent observation of surface heating.
variable_links.limits: Clear-sky daytime only; spurious cooling after 2020 from Terra orbit drift.

variable_links.statement: Vapour pressure deficit rises with temperature when humidity does not keep pace.
variable_links.limits: Derived from forcing fields.

variable_links.statement: Warming reduces snow accumulation and advances melt.
variable_links.limits: Modelled snowpack; not valid over glaciers and ice sheets.

unanswerable_notes: Hot days, warm nights and other threshold-based temperature indices need daily data, which is not prepared.

phenomena.label: Heatwave
phenomena.description: A period of consecutive days with temperature above a high threshold for the place and season.

variable_links.statement: Monthly mean air temperature shows whether the background temperature has risen.
variable_links.limits: Heatwaves are defined from daily temperature exceeding percentile thresholds on consecutive days; a monthly mean cannot identify or count them.

variable_links.statement: Dry soil reduces evaporative cooling and can amplify hot extremes.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Daytime land surface temperature describes surface heating under clear sky.
variable_links.limits: Skin temperature, not air temperature; clear-sky only; Terra orbit drift after 2020.

unanswerable_notes: Heatwave number, duration and intensity need daily maximum or minimum temperature; only monthly means are prepared.
No recorded heatwave event catalogue has been delivered and no heatwave recipe is registered.

phenomena.label: Vegetation greening or browning
phenomena.description: A long-term change in how green the land surface is, from changes in leaf cover, growing season or land use.

variable_links.statement: Satellite vegetation indices are the standard record of greening and browning.
variable_links.limits: Greenness is not biomass or ecosystem health; saturates in dense canopies; missing in polar winter.

variable_links.statement: Water supply is one of the climate drivers of vegetation change, especially in dry regions.
variable_links.limits: Attribution of greening to drivers needs models; a parallel trend is not proof of cause.

variable_links.statement: Temperature is one of the climate drivers of vegetation change, especially in cold regions.
variable_links.limits: Attribution needs models; a parallel trend is not proof of cause.

variable_links.statement: Rising vapour pressure deficit is associated with reduced vegetation growth.
variable_links.limits: Derived from forcing fields.

variable_links.statement: Root-zone water availability limits transpiration and growth in water-limited regions.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

unanswerable_notes: Land-cover change, deforestation area, crop yield and biomass are not prepared.
CO2 fertilisation and land management, major drivers of greening, are not in the catalogue.

phenomena.label: Snowpack decline
phenomena.description: A long-term decrease in the water stored as seasonal snow.

variable_links.statement: Snow water equivalent is the direct measure of water stored in the snowpack.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate; unreliable over glaciers, ice sheets and permanent snow; zero outside the snow season.

variable_links.statement: Warmer winters and springs turn snowfall into rain and advance melt.
variable_links.limits: Monthly mean of a forcing field.

variable_links.statement: Snow accumulation depends on cold-season precipitation.
variable_links.limits: Total precipitation; the snowfall fraction is not prepared.

variable_links.statement: Changes in snow storage shift the timing of runoff.
variable_links.limits: Fixed-baseline monthly anomalies describe overall change; a shift in seasonal timing needs a seasonal analysis that is not a registered recipe.

unanswerable_notes: Snow cover extent, snow depth observations and snowfall are not prepared.
Glacier and ice-sheet mass change is a different phenomenon (see ice_mass_loss).

phenomena.label: Terrestrial water storage / groundwater depletion
phenomena.description: A long-term decline in the total water stored on and below the land surface, including aquifers.

variable_links.statement: GRACE terrestrial water storage is the observation used to detect regional water storage loss.
variable_links.limits: About 300 km resolution; the anomaly sums groundwater, soil moisture, snow, ice and surface water and cannot name the component.

variable_links.statement: Modelled soil moisture is one of the components removed from terrestrial water storage to estimate groundwater change.
variable_links.limits: The subtraction itself is not a registered recipe here; the model has no irrigation or groundwater.

variable_links.statement: Snow is one of the storage components included in the terrestrial water storage anomaly.
variable_links.limits: Modelled; not valid over glaciers.

variable_links.statement: Storage changes follow the balance of precipitation, evapotranspiration and runoff; natural variability explains part of the observed trends.
variable_links.limits: A water-balance closure is not computed.

variable_links.statement: Evapotranspiration is the main loss term of the land water balance.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

unanswerable_notes: Groundwater storage itself is not delivered: separating it from terrestrial water storage needs an approved recipe and surface-water data, neither of which is registered.
Well levels, pumping volumes and land subsidence are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Ice sheet and glacier mass loss
phenomena.description: A long-term loss of mass from ice sheets and glaciers.

variable_links.statement: Satellite gravimetry measures mass change, which over ice sheets and glaciated regions is dominated by ice.
variable_links.limits: About 300 km resolution; includes the glacial isostatic adjustment correction error; hydrology gain factors must not be applied to ice.

unanswerable_notes: Glacier area, length, elevation change and ice velocity are not prepared.
The modelled snow water equivalent (swe) is not valid over ice and must not be used here.

phenomena.label: Atmospheric dryness / evaporative demand
phenomena.description: An increase in how much water the atmosphere can take up from soil, plants and open water.

variable_links.statement: Vapour pressure deficit is the direct measure of atmospheric dryness.
variable_links.limits: Derived from forcing fields.

variable_links.statement: Potential evapotranspiration expresses evaporative demand as a water flux.
variable_links.limits: Model diagnostic with a known trend drift in GLDAS-2.1.

variable_links.statement: Temperature raises the saturation vapour pressure and so the demand.
variable_links.limits: Forcing field.

variable_links.statement: Wind speed is one of the four drivers of evaporative demand.
variable_links.limits: Forcing field; speed only.

variable_links.statement: Solar radiation supplies the energy for evaporation.
variable_links.limits: Forcing field.

variable_links.statement: Net radiation is the energy available for evaporation.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

variable_links.statement: Actual evapotranspiration responds to demand only where water is available.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

unanswerable_notes: No aridity index (precipitation ÷ potential evapotranspiration) or climate classification is registered as a recipe.
Pan evaporation and humidity observations are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Soil moisture drying or wetting
phenomena.description: A long-term change in the water held in the soil.

variable_links.statement: Root-zone soil moisture is the storage that plants and evapotranspiration depend on.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Surface soil moisture shows the fast response of the top soil layer.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters. 1° product.

variable_links.statement: Soil moisture of the whole column shows the slower, deeper response.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Root-zone degree of saturation from an independent reanalysis land model.
variable_links.limits: A different quantity (0–1) from storage in millimetres; reported separately, never merged.

variable_links.statement: Precipitation is the supply of soil moisture.
variable_links.limits: Monthly regional mean.

variable_links.statement: Evapotranspiration is the main loss of soil moisture and is itself limited by it.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

variable_links.statement: Atmospheric demand increases the loss of soil water.
variable_links.limits: Derived from forcing fields.

variable_links.statement: Vegetation growth is reduced under water stress.
variable_links.limits: Greenness also responds to land use and irrigation.

unanswerable_notes: Satellite soil moisture retrievals (e.g. SMAP) and in situ soil moisture are not prepared; all soil moisture here is modelled.

phenomena.label: Water cycle change
phenomena.description: A long-term change in the fluxes and stores of water on land: precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff and storage.

variable_links.statement: Precipitation is the input of the land water balance.
variable_links.limits: Monthly regional mean.

variable_links.statement: Evapotranspiration is the main return flux to the atmosphere.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

variable_links.statement: Runoff is the water the land supplies to rivers.
variable_links.limits: Modelled runoff generation, not gauged discharge.

variable_links.statement: Terrestrial water storage integrates the imbalance of the fluxes.
variable_links.limits: About 300 km resolution; includes human withdrawals.

variable_links.statement: Soil moisture responds to the balance of precipitation and evapotranspiration.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Snow storage changes the seasonal timing of water availability.
variable_links.limits: Modelled; not valid over glaciers.

unanswerable_notes: Gauged river discharge, reservoir storage and water use are not prepared.
The water balance is not closed by the system: products come from different sources and are analysed one by one.

phenomena.label: Ocean warming / marine heatwave
phenomena.description: A long-term rise of sea surface temperature, and discrete periods of anomalously warm water (marine heatwaves).

variable_links.statement: Sea surface temperature is the variable in which ocean surface warming and marine heatwaves are defined.
variable_links.limits: Monthly means describe warming; a marine heatwave is defined on daily data against a 90th-percentile threshold for at least five days and cannot be counted from monthly means.

unanswerable_notes: Marine heatwave frequency, duration and intensity need daily sea surface temperature; only monthly means are prepared and no recipe is registered.
Subsurface temperature, ocean heat content and coral bleaching records are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Wildfire-prone conditions
phenomena.description: Weather and fuel conditions that favour the ignition and spread of vegetation fires. Fire itself is not observed by any prepared variable.

variable_links.statement: Vapour pressure deficit is a measure of fuel aridity that is related to burned area in forests.
variable_links.limits: Shown for western US forests; the relation differs by region and fuel type.

variable_links.statement: Temperature contributes to fuel aridity.
variable_links.limits: Monthly mean of a forcing field.

variable_links.statement: Low precipitation dries fuels.
variable_links.limits: Monthly regional mean.

unanswerable_notes: Burned area, active fire counts and fire emissions are not prepared: fire occurrence, frequency and severity cannot be answered.
No fire-weather index is registered as a recipe; such indices need daily weather.
Ignition sources and fuel load are not in the catalogue.

phenomena.label: Monsoon and rainy-season variability
phenomena.description: Year-to-year and long-term changes in the seasonal rains of monsoon regions.

variable_links.statement: Monsoon regions and monsoon strength are characterised by the seasonal contrast of precipitation.
variable_links.limits: The main analysis removes the fixed seasonal cycle, so its trend describes overall wetting or drying, not a change in onset, withdrawal or seasonal contrast.

variable_links.statement: Soil moisture follows the seasonal rains.
variable_links.limits: Land surface model estimate without irrigation or groundwater; levels depend on model soil parameters.

variable_links.statement: Runoff follows the seasonal rains.
variable_links.limits: Modelled runoff generation.

unanswerable_notes: Monsoon onset and withdrawal dates need daily or pentad data, which is not prepared.
Circulation-based monsoon indices need wind direction and upper-air fields; only near-surface wind speed is prepared.
No recipe for seasonal totals or seasonality change is registered.

phenomena.label: Surface solar radiation change (dimming / brightening)
phenomena.description: Decadal changes in the solar radiation that reaches the surface, caused by clouds and aerosols.

variable_links.statement: Downward shortwave radiation at the surface is the variable in which dimming and brightening are described.
variable_links.limits: Forcing field from analyses and satellite-based radiation whose sources change during the record; not a surface radiometer record.

variable_links.statement: Net radiation responds to changes in incoming solar radiation.
variable_links.limits: Model estimate.

unanswerable_notes: Aerosol optical depth and cloud cover, the causes of dimming and brightening, are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Near-surface wind speed change (stilling)
phenomena.description: A long-term change of wind speed near the surface.

variable_links.statement: Near-surface wind speed is the variable in which stilling is described.
variable_links.limits: Analysis-based forcing field, not an anemometer record; published stilling trends come from station observations and may not appear in analyses.

variable_links.statement: Wind speed is one of the drivers of evaporative demand.
variable_links.limits: Model diagnostic with a known trend drift.

unanswerable_notes: Wind direction, gusts and storms are not prepared.

phenomena.label: Dust, aerosol and air quality
phenomena.description: Particles suspended in the air from deserts, fires and human activity.
unanswerable_notes: No aerosol optical depth, dust, particulate matter or trace-gas product is prepared: this phenomenon cannot be analysed with the current data.
Wind speed, soil moisture or vegetation must not be presented as a dust or air-quality trend.

phenomena.label: Sea level rise
phenomena.description: A long-term rise of the sea surface height.
unanswerable_notes: No sea surface height or tide-gauge product is prepared (the region catalogue names a sea-level category, but no series is delivered).
Sea surface temperature is not a sea-level measurement.

phenomena.label: Sea ice decline
phenomena.description: A long-term decrease of the area or thickness of sea ice.
unanswerable_notes: No sea ice concentration, extent or thickness product is prepared (the region catalogue names a sea-ice category, but no series is delivered).
Sea surface temperature in ice-covered months is constrained by the ice analysis of the source product and must not be used as a sea-ice indicator.

phenomena.label: Tropical cyclones
phenomena.description: Intense rotating storms over warm oceans.

variable_links.statement: Tropical cyclones form over warm ocean water.
variable_links.limits: Warm sea surface is a background condition, not a count or intensity of storms; many other factors control cyclone activity.

unanswerable_notes: Cyclone frequency, tracks and intensity need a storm track catalogue, which has not been delivered.
Monthly precipitation or wind speed cannot identify individual storms.
